run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:07:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by an availability gap of the ad service that began with an ad Deployment rollout at 13:08:26-13:08:28 and lasted until roughly 13:18. The old ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was killed and the replacement pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was reported Ready immediately (the pod template has no readiness probe), but its container did not handle any gRPC requests until ~13:18:16. frontend's client call grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP:8080), so frontend's /api/data route returned HTTP 500 and frontend-proxy emitted error ing/egress spans with http.status_code 500. frontend-proxy error-span rate rose from a ~0.004-0.015/s baseline to a peak of ~2.05/s at 13:14:00 and returned near baseline by 13:22:06; only frontend and frontend-proxy show elevated error spans, which is consistent with frontend-proxy being the edge and frontend the caller, while the ad service's own spans show no errors. The alert's own rule expression is not available in the queried Prometheus, and its firing instant 13:07:06 precedes the sustained burst (~13:09-13:10), where only sporadic 2-4 error spans/min occurred; that timing relationship remains unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy produced error spans on both its operations: whole-window (12:07:06-13:31:18) increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total was 427.19 ERROR spans for span_name 'ingress' and 393.71 ERROR spans for span_name 'router frontend egress', against 24393.53 and 24426.00 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans respectively.

The frontend-proxy error-span rate (span_name ingress, STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was ~0.004-0.015/s up to 13:09:06, rose through 0.40/s at 13:10:06 to a peak of 2.05/s at 13:14:06, stayed ~1.3-1.7/s to 13:18:06, then decayed to 0.0148/s at 13:22:06. The 'router frontend egress' series follows the same shape.

Per-minute increase of frontend-proxy error spans shows sporadic 2-4 spans/min at 13:02, 13:04 and 13:07, then 108 error spans in the minute ending 13:10:00 and 90-122 per minute through 13:16:00, so the sustained burst starts at about 13:09.

In a sample of frontend traces with error=true, the call chain visible through parent references is load-generator GET (http.status_code 500) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' error span (http.status_code 500) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' error span (500) -> frontend GET error span (500) -> frontend 'GET /api/data' (500) -> frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' (500) -> frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with rpc.grpc.status_code 14, whose error detail reads '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'.

Within 13:05:00-13:31:18, frontend error spans are confined to the /api/data path: increase was 403.15 for span_name 'GET', 403.15 for 'GET /api/data', 403.15 for 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', 403.33 for 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' and 15.59 for 'tcp.connect', while 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', 'POST /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' all had error increase 0.

At service level over 12:50:00-13:31:18, only frontend (peak 4.08 error spans/s at 13:15:00) and frontend-proxy (peak 2.05/s) show elevated ERROR span rates; accounting, ad, fraud-detection, payment and recommendation stayed at 0 or ~0.0037 error spans/s.
The refused address in the error text is the ad Service: Service 'ad' in namespace otel-demo has clusterIP 100.70.197.56 and port 8080 (targetPort 8080).

Deployment 'ad' in otel-demo was rolled out during the window: events show Scheduling/Created/Started of pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh at 13:08:26-13:08:28, 'Created pod: ad-785b4464f5' (SuccessfulCreate) at 13:08:26, Deployment 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' at 13:08:26, and at 13:08:28 'Stopping container ad' on pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc, 'SuccessfulDelete' of that pod by ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0'.

The ad Deployment pod template has containerPort 8080 and env AD_PORT=8080, and both readinessProbe and livenessProbe are null; the container has cpu limit 50m and memory limit 450Mi, and the Deployment is at metadata.generation 2 with annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 and replicas 1.

The replacement pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh reports phase Running with Ready condition lastTransitionTime 13:08:28Z, restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, i.e. no crash or restart; the log tool notes it has no previous container instance.
The ad Service's only endpoint during and after the event is pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh at 100.96.3.224:8080 (single address), so the whole ad backend depended on that one pod.

The ad service's own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds shows an outage coincident with the frontend failures: 5-minute rate fell from 1.02/s at 13:09:00 to 0.0037/s at 13:14:00, was exactly 0 at 13:15:00, 13:16:00 and 13:17:00, and recovered to 0.26/s at 13:18:00 and 0.41/s at 13:19:00 (internal spans getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds follow the same pattern).

All 340 ad container log lines available for pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh in the 13:05:00-13:31:00 window begin at 13:18:16.444Z and are per-request lines ('Targeted ad request received for ...', 'Non-targeted ad request received ...', 'no baggage found in context'), so the container logged no handled requests between its 13:08:28 start and 13:18:16.

The likely cause of the frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is the ad Deployment rollout at 13:08:26-13:08:28: because the ad pod template has no readiness probe, the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was declared Ready at 13:08:28 while its container was not yet accepting connections on 8080, and the controller then terminated the only previously serving pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc, leaving the ad Service endpoint refusing connections until about 13:18. frontend's GetAds calls then failed with ECONNREFUSED on the ad ClusterIP, /api/data returned HTTP 500, and frontend-proxy returned 500 on its ingress and frontend-egress spans.

The ~10 minute delay between container start (13:08:28) and first served request (13:18:16) may be slow application start-up aggravated by the 50m CPU limit on the ad container; the evidence shows the delay but cannot attribute it to CPU throttling.

A remaining, unconfirmed contributor to the tail of the burst is frontend's gRPC channel state: frontend error spans continue at a declining rate from 13:18:06 (0.70/s) to 13:21:06 (0.10/s) while the ad service has already resumed serving spans at 13:18-13:19, which is consistent with client-side reconnect/backoff but is not proven by the evidence available.

The ad service shows no self-reported errors: its span error rate stayed at 0/~0.0037 during the incident, and its replacement pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh has restartCount 0 with no previous container instance, so no OOMKill, crash or restart occurred on that pod; the failure was connectivity to a pod that was running and Ready but not yet serving.

The frontend and frontend-proxy workloads themselves were running without restarts (frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw and frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl both restartCount 0, both Deployments Available with 1 ready replica), and only the /api/data -> GetAds operation failed, so the alert is not caused by a failure of the frontend-proxy container or of the frontend container's other routes.

fraud-detection is not a cause of this alert: its pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 was OOMKilled at 12:43:04Z (exit code 137, restartCount 1), which is ~25 minutes before the burst, and its span error rate stayed at 0/~0.0037 during the incident with no errors on the checkout path.

Add a readiness probe (or gRPC/HTTP health check) on port 8080 to the ad Deployment's container so a restarting pod is only added to the ad Service endpoints after it actually listens, and consider raising the 50m CPU limit for faster start-up; a probe would have kept the old pod serving until the new one was actually ready.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the alert's expression, evaluation window and the '2.4555555555555553' value cannot be verified; the alert's firing instant 13:07:06Z also precedes the sustained error burst that starts about 13:09.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count has no series in 13:05-13:31 (get_series and get_all_labels both returned no data), so the request-rate denominator behind the alert value is unknown.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count / rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket produced no series (get_metric_names for rpc_.* returned no data), so gRPC status-code series cannot be used; gRPC status 14 is known only from the sampled span tags.

kube_pod_container_info for ad-* pods returned no series, so the image digests of the old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc and the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh cannot be compared; whether the 13:08:26 rollout was config-only or an image change is unknown.
The old ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc no longer exists, so its logs and its last serving time are unavailable; the exact moment ad stopped answering is bounded only by metrics (~13:09).
Frontend pod logs returned no lines for 13:05-13:31 (status no_data), so frontend-side application error lines and the duration of any gRPC channel backoff cannot be confirmed.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so what or who triggered the ad Deployment update at 13:08:26 (revision 2) is unknown.
next_steps: Add a readinessProbe (gRPC health or TCP 8080) to the otel-demo ad Deployment and review its CPU limit (50m) so rolling updates cannot remove the only serving pod before the replacement is actually listening.
Review the change record for the otel-demo ad Deployment revision 2 at 2026-11-16T13:08:26Z (change-history integration not available here) to confirm the intent of that rollout.
Check frontend's gRPC client settings (retry/backoff, channel re-resolution) to shorten the tail of 500s after the ad backend recovers.

Alert-rule hygiene: confirm the definitions behind RequestErrorRate (expression and window) in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration that actually owns the rule, since the queried Prometheus has no rule of that name.

view.incomplete_reason: backend returned as many traces as requested; more may exist
